access_boundary: This record represents the AikidoSec/altar-1 Altar-1 release announced September 21, 2026. The zai-org/GLM-5.3 parent release, the cyankiwi/GLM-5.3-AWQ-INT4 quantization base, 0xSero's sibling 569B and EXL3 cuts of the same expert selection, the Aikido Machine on-prem appliance, the Aikido Attack, Code Audit, and Deep Review products, and any hosted inference endpoint remain separate boundaries.

evidence.label: Official Aikido Altar announcement: method, storage, evaluation, and serving
Developer-published AikidoSec/altar-1 weights repository and model card
GLM-5.3 License file inherited by Altar-1, with model-as-a-service security-review clause

license_evidence.scope: AikidoSec/altar-1 weights, configuration, tokenizer, and documentation by inheritance of the GLM-5.3 License; the Altar-1 repository ships no separate license file. Hosted Aikido products and services are governed separately.

license_note: The AikidoSec/altar-1 model card states the release inherits the GLM-5.3 license rather than shipping its own license file. The governing text is the zai-org/GLM-5.3 license granting use, copying, modification, distribution, deployment, and fine-tuning, but requiring any licensee operating a model-as-a-service business above 10 billion US dollars in aggregate affiliate revenue over any consecutive twelve months to pass a Z.AI security review before any commercial use. That gate breaks from an open-source posture, so the release is source-available rather than open source.
strengths: Developer-published sharded W4A16 safetensors checkpoint with tokenizer, chat template, and prune plan on the AikidoSec Hugging Face organization, plus a documented vLLM command for a 4xH200 node

First-party announcement and model card document the REAP pruning method, the per-checkpoint storage table, the calibration domains, and an internal 32-vulnerability rediscovery comparison with its pipeline boundaries stated
tradeoffs: The inherited custom GLM-5.3 License gates commercial model-as-a-service use by large operators behind a Z.AI security review
The documented self-hosted path requires Hopper GPUs in a 4xH200 configuration; no developer API or third-party hosted path is documented
No versioning or deprecation posture is stated for the Altar line
